newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey backs down on US Cobra purchase.
newsitem.headline: Turkey backs down on US Cobra purchase.

text.p: Turkey said on Wednesday it had cancelled an order with a U.S. company for 10 Cobra helicopters, whose sale had been delayed by a faction in the U.S. Congress worried the gunships would be used against Kurdish rebels.
"We informed the United States offically that we have decided not to buy the Cobra helicopters," foreign ministry spokesman Sermet Atacanli told reporters.
"Yes, we have been officially notified about that" a U.S embassy official told Reuters. Cobra helicopters are made by Textron Inc's Bell Helicopter.
A Turkish foreign ministry official said Ankara had decided against buying the helicopters after a prolonged delay in their delivery.
U.S- Turkish relations have come under increasing scrutiny and criticism in the U.S. Congress, particularly because of Ankara's treatment of Kurds seeking autonomy.

A coalition of Democrats and Republicans had blocked the normally routine sale of the attack helicopters, saying Turkey might use them to attack Kurdish rebels fighting for autonomy or independence in the country's mainly Kurdish southeast.
"We had an agreement. But because of the delay, we decided against taking them," the foreign ministry official told Reuters.
The value of the helicopter deal was unclear and officials in Ankara refused to give further details.
